messages.content: 計算兩個電荷為5C和7C，相距3米時的電磁力。

function.name: electromagnetic_force
function.description: Calculate the electromagnetic force between two charges placed at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge1.description: The magnitude of the first charge in coulombs.

charge2.description: The magnitude of the second charge in coulombs.

distance.description: The distance between the two charges in meters.

medium_permittivity.description: The relative permittivity of the medium in which the charges are present. Default is 8.854e-12 (Vacuum Permittivity). This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user wants to calculate the electromagnetic force between two charges of 5C and 7C, separated by 3 meters. They didn't specify the medium permittivity, so we use default vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m. Use Coulomb's law: F = k * q1 * q2 / r^2, where k = 1/(4πϵ0). But we can also compute using the given function. The function signature: electromagnetic_force({charge1, charge2, distance, medium_permittivity?}). The function expects the relative permittivity of the medium? Wait: The description says "relative permittivity of the medium in which the charges are present. Default is 8.854e-12 (Vacuum Permittivity)." That seems wrong: relative permittivity is dimensionless, but they say default is 8.854e-12, which is vacuum permittivity. So they likely mean absolute permittivity. So we pass medium_permittivity=8.854e-12. The function will compute the force. We need to call the function.
